# Locale debounce postpones manager updates while notification cache writes continue

Fresh complete two-file124-line patch and every changed test hunk read. Each app-locale observer event clears/replaces a five-second timeout; the callback clears its handle before reevaluating notifications. While a locale timeout is pending, _updateNotificationManager returns before both scheduling the next candidate and notifying the manager. It is a scoped debounce of locale eligibility, not a general arbitrary-delay test practice. Fixed updateNotifications still replaces the raw notification cache, cleans state as requested and calls saveSoon even when the manager update returns early for locale debounce. Awaiting that method therefore does not guarantee an immediate manager event or visible notification during the pending interval, and saveSoon is not immediate durable persistence. Existing future-candidate timing lesson04f51 is reused; no duplicate scheduling rule is created. The new guard test sets a truthy dummy handle to simulate pending state, then asserts no event and no next-candidate timer. It does not by itself test timeout replacement or elapsed five-second behavior. The locale test actually changes requestedLocales, waits for a different notification ID and restores state by manually clearing the restoration debounce. These are source assertions, not executed tests.

Scope: Notification locale/cache completion.
